title: Documentation: ctlv: Add userspace ABI
overview: Documentation-only patch that publishes the CTLV userspace ABI as one RST document, links it into the userspace-api index and adds it to the CTLV MAINTAINERS entry. The document describes what the UAPI header (patch 2) defines, what the core (patches 5-12) implements and what the root family (patch 3) exposes; the family-writer guide follows in patch 13.

files.purpose: The normative userspace ABI for CTLV: devices, discovery, wire format, the single ioctl, queries, events, blobs, introspection and limits. It is prose and diagrams only; names come from include/uapi/linux/ctlv.h (patch 2) and the root family spec (patch 3), and behaviour from the core patches 5-12.

units.title: Title and introduction
units.summary: States what CTLV is and what the document covers: one char device per instance, one ioctl, read() for events.
units.details: Points to Documentation/ctlv/specs for per-family contents and to the driver-api guide (patch 13) for family authors. The YAML-to-generator flow is patch 1 (generator) and patch 3 (generated root family).

units.title: Why a TLV transport
units.summary: Rationale: one ioctl for all operations, optional/required attributes, unknown-attribute policy and pre-callback validation.
units.details: The validation promised here is done by message input handling (patch 5) and the schema validator (patch 7) before the dispatch in patch 12 invokes a family callback.

units.title: Devices and access modes
units.summary: Each instance is a /dev/ctlvN node in the ctlv class; the open mode determines observation versus full-control authority.
units.details:
- O_RDONLY is observation, O_RDWR full control, O_WRONLY gives -EACCES.
- Per-operation authority is `read` or `read-write`; events are available to both.
- Event subscriptions and queues are per open file description (patch 10); the open path and class registration are in patch 12.

units.title: Discovery and udev matching
units.summary: Uevents carry CTLV_FAMILY and numbered CTLV_COMPATIBLE_n properties, with a listen-before-enumerate procedure and udev rule examples.
units.details:
- The compatible list is the family ancestry from the root; indices never move, so reparenting a family is an ABI break.
- families-dump on an open fd is the authoritative answer; uevent properties serve pre-open matching only.
- The properties are emitted by the device registration code in patch 12.

units.title: Wire format - attribute header and rules
units.summary: Defines struct ctlv_attr (len, flags, attr_id), 8-byte alignment, how len and padding nest, the root attribute, scalar encodings and the depth limit.
units.details: Mirrors struct ctlv_attr, CTLV_ALIGN, CTLV_ATTR_F_NESTED and CTLV_ATTR_ROOT in the UAPI header (patch 2). Parsing and bounds checks of these rules are in the input path (patch 5); output building is patch 8.

units.title: Wire format - worked message example
units.anchor: A whole message with every offset
units.summary: A complete 120-byte request with offsets and a nested diagram, showing that padding is counted by the parent's len and never by a leaf's own.
units.details: Walking a nest's children advances by CTLV_ALIGN(child.len); walking a single payload advances by child.len.

units.title: Attribute and operation IDs
units.anchor: An attribute ID names the family
units.summary: 64-bit IDs pack family, group and attribute (operations: family and op), built with the CTLV_ATTR and CTLV_OP macros.
units.details: These macros are in the UAPI header (patch 2); the per-family complete IDs are produced by the generator (patch 1), e.g. for the root family in patch 3.

units.title: Request occurrence order
units.summary: Occurrences of one attribute ID must be contiguous in a nest; an ignored unknown attribute ends a run.

units.title: Attributes a kernel may skip
units.summary: CTLV_ATTR_F_IGNORE_IF_UNKNOWN lets a request carry attributes an older kernel has never heard of, without weakening validation of known IDs.
units.details:
- Applies only to requests, never to the root, replies or events.
- An ID the schema declares elsewhere is still validated, so the bit forgives only complete IDs unknown to every family of the device.
- Callers use op-schema-get to learn which attributes were understood. Implemented in patch 7.

units.title: Executing an operation - ioctl structure
units.summary: The single ioctl CTLV_IOC_OP_EXEC and struct ctlv_op_exec, with the meaning of request_len/reply_len as copy boundaries and the request-root requirement.
units.details:
- The struct and ioctl number are in the UAPI header (patch 2); handling is in patches 5, 8 and 12.
- reserved[] must be zero for compatible growth; generation and cursor are for queries only.
- request-max-len from ops-dump is computed from the known schema; unknown ignorable attributes may exceed it up to the 1 MiB transport limit.

units.title: Operation kinds
units.summary: Distinguishes action, query and event operations by what they answer.
units.details: Kinds are declared in the family YAML and surfaced by ops-dump; dispatch is in patch 12.

units.title: Errors
units.summary: Describes the TLV error information written to the reply buffer and the meaning of each errno returned by the ioctl and by read().
units.details: The error TLV uses the validation-reason and related attributes of the root family (patch 3), written by the output code (patch 8). The errno is authoritative if the buffer is too small.

units.title: Queries and fragments
units.summary: Explains multi-call query replies using generation and cursor, FRAG_MORE on the root and open nests, and reassembly.
units.details:
- First call has generation and cursor zero; a nonzero returned cursor means more to come.
- Continuations must repeat op_id and request; a stale generation gives -ESTALE.
- Readers must reject non-progress or a repeated cursor. The fragmenting writer is in the output patch (8).

units.title: Events - subscription, record format and queue
units.summary: Events are subscribed per file description, read as one record (header plus one root) per read(), with sequence numbers and overflow reporting.
units.details:
- struct ctlv_event_hdr is in the UAPI header (patch 2); queue, sequence numbering and event-overflow records are in patch 10.
- Subscriptions use the subscriptions-add/remove actions and queue size is managed by event-queue-get/set from the root family (patch 3).

units.title: Events - root family events
units.anchor: Two events come from the root family
units.summary: Documents op-changed and device-removed, the two events defined by the root family.
units.details: op-changed carries the same state generation as ops-dump so clients can order dump against event (patch 11); device-removed is emitted at unregistration (patch 12).

units.title: Blobs
units.summary: Large data is passed by blob descriptor (backing type, length, identifier); only the anonymous userspace VA backing is defined, with lifetime and aliasing rules.
units.details: Descriptor validation is patch 6 and VA acquire/release around the callback is patch 9. Caller must not touch input blobs, or access output/inout blobs, while the operation is in flight.

units.title: Introspection
units.summary: The core answers families-dump, ops-dump and op-schema-get on every device so a program can discover a device without compile-time knowledge.
units.details:
- The queries are defined in the root family (patch 3) and implemented by the introspection code (patch 11).
- Recursive schemas are reported with schema.reenters, counting how many levels up the re-entered level is.
- ops-dump lengths include descendant-family additions, so callers should ask rather than compute.

units.title: Limits
units.summary: Implementation limits for message size, error length, nesting, default query buffer and event queue.
units.details: Stated as implementation limits rather than wire maxima so raising them later is compatible. The constants are CTLV_MAX_INLINE_MESSAGE_LEN, CTLV_MAX_ERROR_LEN, CTLV_MAX_NEST_DEPTH, CTLV_DEFAULT_QUERY_REPLY_LEN and CTLV_MAX_EVENT_QUEUE_LEN in the UAPI header (patch 2).
